entries.name: The Choir
entries.heard: A hundred voices hold one note and a quiet voice under it counts.
entries.text: A hundred voices hold one note, and under it a quieter voice counts: one lamp, five gears, three keys. The note is a place. The place is the Last Lamp, and it answers only to three voices.

entries.name: Undertow
entries.heard: A pulsar ticks steadily. Between ticks something else ticks too.
entries.text: A pulsar ticks once every second and a half. Between its ticks a smaller tick keeps time with it and never drifts. Whoever winds the Lamp must wind the smallest gear first and the largest last.

entries.name: The Tally
entries.heard: A ledger read aloud by a machine, goods in and goods out, over and over.
entries.text: A census broadcast from a world with nobody left to read it. Goods in, goods out, balanced to the grain. It ends with a single debt: one lamp, owed since before the lanes were cut.

entries.name: The Psalm
entries.heard: A hymn in parts, sung by instruments rather than throats.
entries.text: A hymn in four parts. Each names an arm of the Orrery and what it owes. The fifth part is silence, and the silence is marked as a rest rather than an ending.

entries.name: Ember Call
entries.heard: A distress loop. The voice is calm in the way people are when they are not.
entries.text: A warship's distress loop, still afraid after all this time. It asks for nothing except a light to steer by. It gives its drive logs in thanks, and with them a shorter way across the dark.

entries.name: Beacon Echo
entries.heard: One bright pulse, repeated, from a light you did not know you had built.
entries.text: A single bright pulse, repeated, from a beacon built far away on solid ground. It is asking whether anyone saw it. Someone did. The reply is a coordinate and a thank-you.
